2700:
** κατατοξ-εύω**,
**strike down with arrows, shoot dead**, τινα [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.36, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.34, etc.; ῥηματίοισιν καινοῖς αὐτὸν καὶ διανοίαις κ. Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Nubes” 944}}]:—_passive_, [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “HG” 4.7.6, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Piet.” 34: _metaphorically_, κ. τινὰ τὸ περιττὸν τῆς τρυφῆς Eunapius Historicus [{4-5th c.AD}] “Fragmenta Historica - HGM” p.263 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator}}]
2705:
** καταφῐλ-έω**,
**kiss, caress**, δίφρον {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.4.10}}; χεῖρας καὶ πόδας τινός{{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. work] 7.5.32, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 56, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 4.10.20}}; τοὺς μὲν καλοὺς φιλήσοντος, τοὺς δ᾽ ἀγαθοὺς καταφ. {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.6.33, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 553, LXX.Ruth.1.9, NT.Matt.26.49}}; distinct from φιλεῖν, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.478}}; especially of an amorous kiss. {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 13.}}
2707:
** καταφρον-ητής**, οῦ, ὁ,
**despiser**, νόμων {{LXX+1st c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 4.7.33; θανάτου 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Brutus” 12; πλούτου 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 2.8.3: _absolutely_, LXX.Hab.1.5, LXX.Zeph.3.4, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 47.33.}}
2709:
** καταχθόν-ιος**, ον,
also η, ον {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1413}}:— **subterranean**, Ζεὺς καταχθόνιος, i.e. Pluto, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.457 (but Ζεὺς κ., = “Veiouis”, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.10)}}; of Pluto, Demeter, Persephone, and the Erinyes, {{Refs 4th c.AD+|“IG” 3.1423; δαίμονες κ. 4th c.AD(?): Hierocles Facetiarum Scriptor “in CA” I p.419}} M.; = Latin _Di Manes,_ {{Refs|Anthologia Graeca 7.333}}; κ.θεοί, = Latin _Di Manes_, frequently in sepulchral Inscrr., {{Refs|“IG” 14.1660, +others}}
2712:
** κατείδωλος**, ον,
**full of idols, given to idolatry,** {{NT|NT.Acts.17.16.}}
2713:
Included with: ** κατ-έναντα**,
_adverb_ **over against, opposite**, with _genitive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC(?): Cydias Lyricus 1, 2nd c.AD: Pancrates Epicus “POxy.” 1085.24, 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 1.552, 4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 3.176: with _dative_, [prev. author] 6.277: _absolutely_, [prev. author] 3.132}}:—also **κατ-έναντι** {{LXX|LXX.Exo.19.2}}; πύλη ἡ κ.{{LXX+NT+2nd c.BC+|LXX.Eze.11.1; κώμη ἡ κ. ὑμῶν NT.Mark.11.2, compare “UPZ” 79.11 (2nd c.BC), “Inscription Prien.” 37.170 (2nd c.BC).}}
2714:
** κατένωπα**
{{Refs 2nd c.AD+|compare (2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus Gr. 2.94}}, κατενῶπα or κατ᾽ ἐνῶπα {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristarchus Grammaticus cited in Hdn.Gr.[same place])}}, **over against, right opposite**, c._genitive_, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.320, 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Lithica” 132, 464: with _accusative_, Puchstein “epigram Gr.” p.76 (from Memphis)}}:—also**κατεν-ενώπιον**, τινος {{LXX+NT+6th c.AD+|LXX.Josh.1.5, NT.Eph.1.4, +others, “BGU” 954.6 (6th c.AD).}}.
Included with: ** κατεξᾰγιάζω**,
**assay,** {{Refs|Arch.Anz. 38/39.154 (_passive_).}}
2715:
** κατεξ-ουσιάζω**,
**exercise authority over**, τινος {{NT+4th c.AD+|NT.Matt.20.25, NT.Mark.10.42; τῶν ὅλων 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “contra Galilaeos” 100c.}}
2721:
** κατεφίσταμαι**,
**rise up against**, in _aorist_ _active_, κατεπέστησαν τῷ Παύλῳ {{NT|NT.Act.18.12.}}
2725:
** κατήγορ-ος**, ὁ,
**accuser**, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.71, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 814, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.16, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.11, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18a (_plural_), NT.Rev.12.10, etc.}}; δημόσιος κ. public **prosecutor,** {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|PFlor. 6.6 (3rd c.AD)}}; **betrayer**, φρονημάτων ἡ γλῶσσ᾽ ἀληθὴς γίγνεται κ. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 439; ἀμέλειά ἐστι σαφὴς ψυχῆς κ. κακῆς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 20.15}}; πνεῦμα ὧν κατήγορον,.. δρόμοις [ἡ φύσις] ἐκβιᾶται κατηγορέειν what the respiration **reveals**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τέχνης” 12.}}
2726:
** κατήφ-εια**,
_Ionic dialect_ and _Epic dialect_ **κατηφ-είη**, ἡ, (κατηφής) **dejection** (λύπη κάτω βλέπειν ποιοῦσα {{Refs 8th c.BC+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.528e), δυσμενέσιν μὲν χάρμα κατηφείην δὲ σοὶ αὐτῷ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.51; κ. καὶ ὄνειδος 16.498, 17.556; κ. τέ τις ἅμα καὶ κατάμεμψις σφῶν αὐτῶν πολλὴ ἦν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.75}}; opposed to χαρά, {{NT+3rd c.BC+|NT.Jam.4.9; δυσθυμία καὶ κ. 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Themistocles” 9; τὴν βουλὴν ἄχος καὶ κ. ἔσχε [prev. author] “Cor.” 20, compare 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 3.19, 1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 28, 2nd c.AD(?): Charito Scriptor Eroticus 6.8; κ. καὶ σύννοια 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.204; κ. καὶ ὀϊζύς 3rd c.BC: Rhianus Epicus 1.8.}}
2728:
** κατῑόομαι**,
_passive_, **become rusty, tarnished**, {{LXX+1st c.BC+|LXX.Sir.12.11 (_active_ is variant), 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 16.2.42, NT.Jam.5.3, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 4.82, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 4.6.14: _metaphorically_, βασιλεία σιδηρᾶ καὶ -ιωμένη 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 71.36.}}
2732:
** κατοικ-ητήριον**, τό,
**dwellingplace, abode**, {{LXX|LXX.Exo.12.20}}; κ. θεοῦ, δαιμονίων, {{NT|NT.Eph.2.22, NT.Rev.18.2.}}
2739:
** καυμᾰτ-ίζω**,
**burn, scorch up,** {{NT|NT.Rev. 16.8}}:—_passive_, **to be burnt up,** {{NT|NT.Matt.13.6}}; **become heated, suffer from heat**, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.100b, 691f, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.6.26, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.108, 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 7.64.}}
2743:
** καυ-τηριάζω**,
**brand**, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 5.1.9}}:—_passive_, {{NT|“Hippiatrica” 1: _metaphorically_, κεκαυτηριασμένοι τὴν ἰδίαν συνείδησιν NT.1Tim.4.2.}}
2744:
** καυχ-άομαι**,
_Doric dialect_ **καυχέομαι** {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 5.77}}; _2nd pers._ _singular_ καυχᾶσαι in late Gr., as {{NT|NT.Rom.2.17, 23, etc.}}: _future_ -ήσομαι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.39, 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 134, 4th c.BC: Epicrates Comicus 6}}: _aorist_ ἐκαυχησάμην {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1311b4}}; _Aeolic dialect_ _optative_ καυχάσαιτο {{Refs 7th c.BC+|7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 4.2}}: _perfect_ κεκαύχημαι {{NT|NT.2Cor.7.14}}:—_active_, {{Refs|“Etymologicum Magnum” 527.1}}:— **speak loud, be loud-tongued**, κ. παρὰ καιρόν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 9.38}}, cf. Eup.[same place], etc.; **boast, vaunt oneself**, ἐπ᾽ αἰζηοῖσι κ. μέγα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Cratinus Comicus 95, compare 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator “fragment” 78; εἴς τι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus}} [same place]; ἔν τινι NT.Rom.[same places]: c._accusative_ et _infinitive_, _aorist_ or _present_, **boast that**.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same place], 4th c.BC: Epicrates Comicus}} [same place], etc.: with _participle_, **boast of** doing or being, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 616, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.30}}; ὅτι.. {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 13.1.27}}: with _accusative_, **boast of**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 141, NT.2Cor.9.2: c._genitive_, ὧν Ἱππίας ἐκαυχᾶτο 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ κακιῶν ί” p.35 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus: with _dative_, κάλλει “Anthologia Graeca” 12.234 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus).}}
2746:
** καύχ-ησις**, εως, ἡ,
**boasting**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Fragmenta” 93, LXX.1Ch.29.13, +others, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ κακιῶν ί” p.27 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.534, NT.Rom.15.17.}}
2747:
**Κενχρεαί** (Rec. Κεχγ-; ν. WH, _App._, 150), -ῶν, αἱ,
**Cenchreæ, a port of Corinth**: Act.18:18, Rom.16:1.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
2752:
** κέλ-ευσμα**
or **κέλ-ευμα** (see. below), ατος, τό, (κελεύω) **order, command**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 235, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 1219 (_plural_)}}, etc.; **call, summons**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 751 (_plural_)}}: in Prose, **word of command** in battle, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.141, 7.16, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 929 (Lyric poetry); ὁ Κύριος ἐν κ. καταβήσεται ἀπ᾽ οὐρανοῦ NT.1Thes.4.16}}; also, the **call** of the κελευστής (which see), which gave the time to the rowers, ἀπὸ ἑνὸς κελεύσματος all at once, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.92, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.15; ἐξ ἑνὸς κελεύματος 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 25}}; ἐκ κελεύματος at **the word of command**, {{LXX+5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 397, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1405; καχάζετε.. ἀπὸ κ. 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 8; στρατεύσονται ἀφ᾽ ἑνὸς κ. LXX.Pro.30.27}}; of the boatswain's **pipe**, κέλευσμα προσαυλεῖν {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” p.15}} K.; also, the **call** of the driver to his horses, κελεύματι μόνον καὶ λόγῳ ἡνιοχεῖται {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 253d}}; of the huntsman to his hounds, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 6.20; κ. κυνηγετῶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ichn.” 225. (κέλευμα}} is the more ancient form, as in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 397, “Ch.” 751, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus (codices [same place]), 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus, [same places], variant in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus [same places], 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus [same place])}}
2755:
** κενόδοξ-ος**, ον,
**vain-glorious, conceited**, {{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 27.7.12, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.672, NT.Gal.5.26, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.24.43, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 6.180d; κληρονομία 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 271.2.}}
2757:
** κενοφων-ία**, ἡ,
**vain talking**, {{NT+1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus “Praef.” 2: in _plural_, NT.1Tim.6.20, NT.2Tim.2.16, 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “adversus Christianos - Abh. Berl. Akad.” 58; ἄγραφοι κ. 6th c.AD: Justinianus Imperator “Novellae” 146.1.2.}}
2760:
** κεντορίων**, ωνος, ὁ,
= Latin _centurio_, {{Refs|“OGI” 196 (from Philae)}}:—also **κεντουρίων**, {{Refs 6th c.AD+|6th c.AD: Lydus, Joannes Laurentius Historicus “Mag.” 1.9}}; **κεντυρίων**, {{NT|NT.Mark.15.39.}}
2764:
** κερᾰμ-ῐκός**, ή, όν,
**of** or **for pottery**, γῆ κ. **potter's** earth, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ τῶν ἐντὸς παθῶν” 7, compare 5th c.BC: Sannyrio Comicus 4}}; κ. ῥύμη, ={Κεραμεικός}, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 4; κ. κέραμος “IG” 42(1).102.281 (Epid., 4th c.BC)}}; ὁ κ. τροχός {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 7.3.9}}; κ. μάστιξ, Comedy texts Phrase for ostracism, {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|“Comica Adespota” 33; ἐργαστήριον “PFlor.” 50.68 (3rd c.AD)}}; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη) **the potter's art, pottery**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 288a}}; see at {κεραμεικός}.
2786:
**Κηφᾶς**, -ᾶ (see Bl., § 10, 3), ὁ (Aram. כֵּיפָא),
Cephas, i.e. Peter: Jhn.1:43, 1Co.1:12 3:22 9:5 15:5, Gal.1:18 2:9, 11 2:14.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
2787:
** κῑβωτός**, ἡ,
**box, chest, coffer**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Hecataeus Milesius Historicus 368 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, 4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 239, 5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 228.4, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1000, “V.” 1056 (_anapaest meter_), 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 12.10, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 18.4, “IG” 22.1388.73; κ. δίθυρος, τετράθυρος, [prev. work]12.330; ἱερά, δημοσία κ., “Inscription Délos” 442 A 2,75 (2nd c.BC)}}; Noah's **ark**, {{LXX|LXX.Gen.6.14}}; the **ark** of {{LXX+2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD(?): Moses Alchemista, LXX.Exo.25.9(10), +others}}; πέπτωκεν εἰς κ. has been deposited in the **archives**, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“UPZ” 126 (3rd c.BC)}}, etc.; opposed to κίστη (which see). (Perh. a variant in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.228, cf. Scholia (at [prev. work]) 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus}} cites κίβος as the _radical_ form.)
2789:
** κῐθαρ-ίζω**,
_Attic dialect_ _future_ -ιῶ {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 141}}: (κίθαρις):— **play the cithara**, φόρμιγγι.. ἱμερόεν κιθάριζε {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 18.570, 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 202; λύρῃ δ᾽ ἐρατὸν κιθαρίζων “hymnus ad Mercurium” 423; ἕρπει ἄντα τῶ σιδάρω τὸ καλῶς κιθαρίσδεν 7th c.BC: Alcman Lyricus 35, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 3.1, “Oec.” 2.13; ᾄδειν καὶ κ. 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Mus.” 7}} K.; κιθαρίζειν οὐκ ἐπίσταμαι I am not a 'high-brow', [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 989, compare 959; ἀρχαῖον εἶν᾽ ἔφασκε τὸ κ. [prev. author] “Nu.” 1357: proverbial, ὄνος κιθαρίζειν πειρώμενος, like{ὄνος πρὸς λύραν} (see. λύρα), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Pseudol.” 7}}]; τὸ κιθαριζόμενον **music composed for the cithara**, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1144d.}}
2791:
**Κιλικία**, -ας, ἡ
**Cilicia, a province of Asia Minor**: Act.6:9 15:23, 41 21:39 22:3 23:34 27:5, Gal.1:21.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
2797:
** κίς**, ὁ,
_genitive_ κιός, _accusative_ κῖν, **weevil**, κεῖνον [τὸν χρυσὸν] οὐ σὴς οὐδὲ κὶς δάπτει {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 222: _accusative_ _plural_ κίας 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 4.15.4. [κῑς Hdn.Gr. 2.925 (_oxytone_, 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 1.383): _genitive_ κῑός Hdn.Gr. 2.674: _accusative_ κῖν 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus [same place]]}}
